title: Designing Dealer Compensation in the Auto-Loan Market: Implications from a Policy Change
authors: Zhenling Jiang; Yanhao “Max” Wei; Tat Y. Chan; Naser Hamdi
eligible_reason: Not eligible. One policy change at a single date (z = 1 for loans after the policy change) studied with descriptive before/after density plots and a structural GMM model of dealer compensation and consumer bargaining. No staggered adoption, no TWFE regression.
design_notes: code.R: Figure 1 densities of consumer rates by z for target vs general banks; structural estimation via simulated moments (Moments(), nleqslv) with loan amount, term, credit score; counterfactual compensation designs. The policy is one lender-side change, so all treated loans share one adoption date.
data_files_note: README.txt: Equifax data under NDA; 'We provide a simulated data that mimic the key variables of the original data'; results will differ from the paper.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); the OpenAlex abstract in data/frame/mksc.jsonl is a one-sentence summary. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
